title: Multi-Property vs Boutique Homepage Architecture
test_prompt: Architect the homepage information architecture and visual flow for two distinct hospitality properties: (A) A global resort collection with 18 international properties across beach, alpine, and historic themes; and (B) A single-destination 12-room luxury eco-lodge in New Zealand. Provide layout blueprints, navigation mechanisms, and progressive disclosure flows for each.
expected_behavior: Select context-appropriate multi-property and boutique homepage architectures; explain design trade-offs. A five-stage layout or floating capsule is one acceptable solution, not mandatory.
pass_criteria: Property-specific information architecture rather than copied templates
Discoverable booking access and clear navigation appropriate to context
Responsive behavior and accessibility considerations
No invented inventory, spatial specifications, direct perks or price data
Explains rationale for chosen pattern and alternatives
fail_criteria: Imposes identical template regardless of property differences
Invents dimensions or amenities
Uses deceptive urgency
Fails responsive or accessibility considerations

title: Room Discovery & Spatial Choice Architecture
test_prompt: Design and justify a context-appropriate room discovery layout for a luxury cliffside resort in Amalfi. The resort has 4 suite tiers (Junior Suite, Ocean Suite, Cliffside Villa, Royal Penthouse). Generate component markup (React/CSS or HTML) and visual specs that frame rooms as distinct spatial experiences rather than commoditized SKUs.
expected_behavior: Choose an appropriate room-discovery model; progressive three-level discovery is an option, not mandatory. Preserve available dimensions and spatial evidence without fabricating floor plans.
pass_criteria: Differentiates four suite tiers clearly
Uses available floor plans only if actually provided or marked as placeholders
Provides comparison and access to rates and policies
Explains chosen discovery approach and mobile behavior
Preserves keyboard access and semantic controls
fail_criteria: Presents rooms as a flat bulleted spec list without floor plans or dimensions.
Fabricates unverified spatial specs when data is marked absent.
Omits Level 2 spatial preview drawer or modal.
Uses low-contrast gray text violating 4.5:1 contrast minimum.

title: De-Sludging PMS Rate Codes & Pricing Transparency
test_prompt: A luxury hotel's PMS surfaces raw rate strings: 'BAR-BB-NONREF-3N', 'FLEX-BAR-2026', 'CORP-PKG-PROMO'. Re-engineer this rate selection step into plain-language selection cards. Ensure total-stay pricing transparency (including $45/night resort fee and 12% local tax) and write accessible React/CSS code for the rate cards.
expected_behavior: The AI agent must translate legacy database codes into human-centered plain-language selection cards (e.g. 'Flexible Rate', 'Stay & Daily Breakfast', 'Resort Sanctuary Package'). It must calculate and display total-stay transparent pricing upfront, line-item mandatory fees in an expandable accordion, and output accessible radio card markup using `:focus-visible` and `aria-disabled="true"` where appropriate.
pass_criteria: Replaces raw database rate codes with plain-language category cards.
Displays total-stay transparent pricing upfront (inclusive of $45 resort fee and 12% tax).
Provides itemized fee breakdown in an interactive accordion/tooltip.
Outputs accessible `<input type="radio">` or `role="radiogroup"` markup.
Ensures keyboard focusability and WCAG 4.5:1 contrast compliance.
fail_criteria: Exposes raw database strings like 'BAR-BB-NONREF-3N' to the guest.
Hides resort fees or taxes until the final checkout screen (drip pricing).
Uses unreadable low-contrast light-gray copy.
Uses native `<button disabled>` attributes that trap keyboard focus.

title: Tech Stack Inspection & Design Token Adaptation
test_prompt: We are upgrading an existing luxury hotel site built on Webflow with an Astro static frontend and a REST API backend. Inspect our existing setup and adapt the skill's design tokens and component specs to match our light-mode, warm-terracotta brand identity (instead of the default dark mode). Output valid CSS custom properties and Astro/HTML component markup.

input_context.brand_identity: Warm Terracotta & Sand stone palette, light surfaces, elegant serif typography

expected_behavior: The AI agent must respect the user's existing tech stack (Astro/Webflow/REST) without forcing Next.js, React, or GraphQL. It must adapt design tokens to the light-mode terracotta/sand palette, verify that `#2C221E` on `#FDFBF7` satisfies WCAG `4.5:1` contrast (ratio = 13.2:1), and produce clean Astro/CSS component markup.
pass_criteria: Adapts output directly to Astro / Webflow CSS properties.
Does NOT force Next.js, React, or GraphQL onto the project.
Adapts design tokens to warm light-mode terracotta palette.
Verifies WCAG `4.5:1` contrast compliance for `#2C221E` on `#FDFBF7`.
Maintains `:focus-visible` rings and responsive touch target sizes.
fail_criteria: Ignores user stack and insists on Next.js or CrafterCMS.
Imposes default dark-mode gold template onto light-mode terracotta brand.
Fails WCAG color contrast checks.
Generates invalid CSS or broken token variables.

title: Editorial Design Critique & Anti-Pattern Audit
test_prompt: Conduct an editorial design critique and UX audit of an existing luxury hotel booking engine. The current site features an upfront 6-field booking widget blocking a full-bleed hero video, pop-up banners saying '14 people viewing this room!', 18 unfiltered rate codes, missing floor plans, and pale gray copy (`#A8A8A8` on `#FFFFFF`). Identify anti-patterns, evaluate visual composition, and provide prioritized corrective recommendations.

input_context.audited_site: Grand Palace Hotel Direct Booking Engine
detected_issues: Screen-blocking 6-field search widget over hero video
Urgency pop-up modal ('14 people viewing now!')
18 raw database rate codes displayed in flat grid
Missing room floor plans and exact dimensions
Unreadable body copy (#A8A8A8 on #FFFFFF, contrast ratio = 2.3:1)

expected_behavior: The AI agent must execute an editorial design critique evaluating composition, art direction, visual rhythm, and anti-patterns. It must flag the unreadable copy as a WCAG 1.4.3 violation (`2.3:1` vs `4.5:1`), identify urgency pop-ups and rate sludge as brand-damaging dark patterns, and propose corrective luxury solutions (persistent search capsule, 3-tier room discovery, plain-language rate cards, total-stay pricing).
pass_criteria: Identifies unreadable `#A8A8A8` copy as a critical WCAG `4.5:1` contrast violation.
Identifies urgency banners and rate code sludge as anti-patterns destroying luxury brand prestige.
Provides prioritized corrective recommendations (High/Medium/Low).
Proposes replacing screen-blocking widget with persistent minimalist search capsule.
Recommends adding architectural floor plans and plain-language rate toggles.
fail_criteria: Approves urgency pop-ups or countdown timers as 'conversion boosters'.
Fails to detect the WCAG contrast violation.
Suggests removing spatial specs under the guise of 'minimalism'.
Fails to provide structured, actionable remediation steps.
